sections.html:
Cullman County is in north central Alabama, with the city of Cullman serving as both county seat and largest city. It covers 755 square miles, 735 of them land and 20 water.

Morgan County lies to the north, Marshall to the northeast, Blount to the east, Walker to the southwest, Winston to the west and Lawrence to the northwest. Interstate 65 runs through, along with U.S. 31, U.S. 231, U.S. 278 and State Routes 67, 69, 91 and 157, and CSX Transportation provides the rail line.

The county is a micropolitan area that belongs to the Birmingham-Hoover-Talladega combined statistical area. Local TV and radio come from both Huntsville and Birmingham, but the county sits in the Birmingham media market.

The Alabama legislature organized Cullman County on January 24, 1877 from parts of Blount, Morgan and Winston counties and named it for Colonel John G. Cullmann. The act set March 6, 1877 as the day residents would pick a county seat.

Two towns competed, Cullman and Milner, and Cullman won the vote 760 to 55. Before settlement, the area had been home for thousands of years to varied Indigenous cultures, and the Cherokee and Choctaw lived here at the time of European contact.

A more recent event shaped the county's building stock: the 2011 Cullman tornado struck on April 27, 2011 during the 2011 Super Outbreak. Repair history after a storm is something a buyer's inspector will ask about.

sections.h2: How fast is Cullman County growing?
sections.html:
Cullman County grew 9.3 percent from 80,406 in 2010 to 87,866 in 2020, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 94,009, up another 7.0 percent.

MeasureCullman County
Population, 202087,866
Population estimate, 202594,009
Households34,723
Housing units39,145
Vacant units11.3%
Owner-occupied homes74.2%
Rental vacancy rate6.4%
Living in rural areas75.6%

The rental vacancy rate of 6.4 percent is lower than the 12.2 percent reported for Calhoun County, so a rental house here is less likely to sit empty for long.

The county's growth curve is long. It had 6,355 people in 1880, 28,321 in 1910, 49,046 in 1950, a dip to 45,572 in 1960, then 61,642 in 1980, 77,483 in 2000 and 87,866 in 2020. The median age is 41.3, with 22.3 percent of residents under 18 and 18.9 percent aged 65 or older, so a good share of sellers are long-time owners with decades of equity in the house.

sections.h2: Which cities, towns and schools are in Cullman County?
sections.html:
Cullman County has four cities, nine towns and three public school systems: Cullman City Schools, Arab City Schools and Cullman County Schools.

  • Cities: Arab (mostly in Marshall County), Cullman, Good Hope and Hanceville.
  • Towns: Baileyton, Berlin, Colony, Dodge City, Fairview, Garden City (partly in Blount County), Holly Pond, South Vinemont and West Point.
  • Census-designated places: East Point and Joppa, the latter partly in Marshall County.

The county system covers unincorporated areas and every municipality except Arab and nearly all of Cullman. Wallace State Community College sits in Hanceville in the south end of the county, opened in 1966 and enrolls around 6,000 students. Private options in Cullman include Cullman Christian School, St. Bernard Preparatory School and Sacred Heart of Jesus Catholic Elementary School.

sections.h2: Which unincorporated communities sit in Cullman County?
sections.html:
Beyond the incorporated places, Cullman County has more than twenty named unincorporated communities, and many sellers live in one of them rather than in a city.

  • A to C: Arkadelphia, Battleground, Birdsong, Black Bottom, Bremen, Brooklyn, Bug Tussle, Corinth and Crane Hill.
  • D to L: Damascus, Jones Chapel and Logan.
  • P to W: Phelan, Simcoe, Spring Hill, Trimble, Vinemont, Walter, Welti, Wilburn and White City.

With 75.6 percent of residents outside urban areas, a house in one of these places is usually reached by a county road and falls under the county school system. Private schools add another layer, including Vinemont Christian Academy in South Vinemont, which serves pre-K through 12th grade.

sections.h2: What is different about alcohol rules in Cullman County?
sections.html: Cullman County is classed as moist: the cities of Cullman, Good Hope and Hanceville allow alcohol sales and are wet, and the rest of the county is dry. It matters if you own a building that a restaurant or shop might use, since the answer depends on which side of the city line the parcel falls.

sections.h2: How does Alabama's annual equalization affect a Cullman County parcel?
sections.html:
Every Alabama county is under an annual reappraisal program that has the assessing official review one-quarter of the county each year. All property in a county gets looked at over a four-year cycle, and any new buildings found during that review get added for the next tax year.

The state says the goal is to smooth out large jumps in value and to keep the tax stream stable for schools, cities, counties and the state. If you want to see which year your area is reviewed, ask the Revenue Commissioner's office.

The Department of Revenue also says property owners should report new improvements or removals by December 31, and that re-roofing, minor repairs and painting do not trigger a new assessment.

sections.h2: How is recording tax split when a Cullman County house sells?
sections.html:
When a deed is recorded in Alabama, two-thirds of the privilege tax goes to the state treasury and one-third goes to the county treasury. The rate is 50 cents for each $500 of value conveyed or fraction of it, set by section 40-22-1.

The probate judge calculates the amount due from the actual purchase price, which must be attested on a Department of Revenue form. A deed that conveys property in two or more counties goes through the department, which sets the value in each county.

The statute includes a few exemptions: corrected deeds, deeds for nominal consideration that perfect title, and mortgage transfers where the mortgage tax is already paid. When a $240,000 sale is recorded, the tax is 480 units times 50 cents, or $240, with the probate office's recording fee added.

sections.h2: When are Cullman County taxes due and when do they go delinquent?
sections.html:
Property tax is due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. After that the state timetable runs February to the probate court, March for the probate court to meet, April for advertising and May for the tax sale.

  • You owe the tax even if no statement comes. Revenue Commissioners mail notices only as a courtesy.
  • A written protest of value goes to the Board of Equalization within 30 days of the valuation notice.
  • Owners 65 or older, permanently and totally disabled, or blind are exempt from the state portion once they claim the exemption.

For sellers with a deadline, the first quarter is the crunch. A house that closes in January or February may have an unpaid bill for the year just ended, which is the kind of item a closing agent looks for.

faqs.q: How many people live in Cullman County, Alabama?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 87,866 residents, and the Census Bureau estimated 94,009 for 2025. That is an increase of 7.0 percent over five years.

faqs.q: What is the largest city in Cullman County?
faqs.a: The city of Cullman is both the largest city and the county seat.
The legislature organized it on January 24, 1877. Cullman beat Milner in the county seat vote, 760 to 55.

faqs.q: Is Cullman County wet or dry?
faqs.a: It is moist. Cullman, Good Hope and Hanceville allow alcohol sales, and the rest of the county is dry.

faqs.q: How is a deed taxed in Cullman County?
faqs.a: Alabama charges 50 cents per $500 of value conveyed, and the probate office collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cullman County house for cash if it needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. We buy houses as they stand, so you do not have to fix anything first. Reach out with the address and we will talk through your situation, including any tax owed.
